hook: An idle Postgres database bills $0 in compute on Neon and $15 a month on PlanetScale's smallest HA cluster. Keep that Neon database awake all month at 0.25 CU and it costs 0.25 × 730 h × $0.106 = $19.35 before storage, more than the cluster it was meant to undercut.

sections.title: PlanetScale rents you a machine; Neon bills the hours it is awake
sections.content:
Both vendors sell Postgres in November 2026, so MySQL versus Postgres no longer decides anything. The clock does.

> PlanetScale: capacity is a cluster you rent. Neon: compute is CU-hours, meaning compute size × hours running on Lakebase Postgres.

Each sentence forbids something.

- **PlanetScale forbids a bill that moves with traffic.** A quiet Sunday costs the same as launch day, and a branch is a second cluster.
- **Neon forbids a flat bill for an awake database.** Every running hour meters; suspended compute is $0.

Each model has a price. PlanetScale's docs say it plainly: there is no free plan. Neon's price is a bill that grows with uptime. Figures below are AWS us-east-1 list prices checked 10 November 2026, or arithmetic on them; nothing is benchmarked.

sections.title: The $0 database out-bills the $15 cluster once it never sleeps
sections.content:
The bottom of each price list:

| Entry | Monthly | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Neon Free | $0 | 100 CU-hours, 1 GB storage per project |
| PlanetScale PS-5, single node | $5 | 1/16 vCPU, 512 MiB |
| PlanetScale PS-5 HA | $15 | 1 primary + 2 replicas |

Now keep a 0.25 CU Neon compute awake all month on Launch: 0.25 × 730 h = 182.5 CU-hours × $0.106 = $19.35, before storage. That is $19.35 − $15 = $4.35 more than PlanetScale's three-node cluster. The vendor that bills idle hours wins on a database that is quiet but never asleep.

```python
# Awake hours/month before 0.25 CU on Neon Launch out-bills PS-5 HA.
CU, RATE, PS5_HA = 0.25, 0.106, 15.00
break_even = PS5_HA / (CU * RATE)
print(f"{break_even:.0f} of 730 hours")  # 566
# Here it breaks: a probe every <5 min blocks suspend, so you bill 730.
```

sections.title: One full CU all month puts Neon Scale above PlanetScale's PS-80
sections.content:
Now one CU, awake all month:

| Option | Formula | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| Neon Launch, 1 CU | 730 × $0.106 | $77.38 |
| Neon Scale, 1 CU | 730 × $0.222 | $162.06 |
| PlanetScale PS-80 HA | flat, arm64 | $148 |

Not identical machines. A CU is about 4 GB RAM; PS-80 is listed at 1 vCPU and 8 GiB plus two replicas. On Scale the break-even is $148 ÷ $0.222 = 667 awake hours out of 730.

Read both lists as penalty tables. Neon's own typical-cost rows answer "how many hours?": intermittent load (140 CU-hours + 1 GB) is $15 on Launch, high load (3,000 CU-hours + 100 GB) is $353 on Launch and $701 on Scale. PlanetScale's SKU ladder answers "which size?", from PS-5 at $15 to PS-2560 at $4,529 HA on arm64.

Neon punishes uptime. PlanetScale punishes the night you paid for and did not use.

sections.title: A branch per pull request is a Neon habit, not a PlanetScale one
sections.content:
On PlanetScale every branch runs on its own dedicated cluster, billed separately and prorated to the millisecond. On Neon a branch is a line item: 10 per project included, then $1.50 per branch-month, prorated hourly.

| 20 branches alive all month | Formula | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| Neon Launch | (20 − 10 included) × $1.50 | $15 + CU-hours |
| PlanetScale, PS-5 HA each | 20 × $15 | $300 |

Millisecond proration helps PlanetScale with short-lived branches: one PS-5 HA branch costs $15 ÷ 730 h ≈ $0.02 per hour. A preview per pull request lives for days, though, and that meter runs whether anyone opens it or not. Neon branch compute bills CU-hours and suspends after five idle minutes, so an unreviewed PR costs a branch fee and storage, not a cluster.

sections.title: PlanetScale's 2026 bets are sharded Postgres in preview and Drizzle's maintainers
sections.content:
Neki is PlanetScale's sharded Postgres, in platform preview since 10 September 2026. Apps reach it through a Neki router over the Postgres wire protocol.

- No single-node configuration: the smallest arm64 shard is PS-10 at $30, 1 primary and 2 replicas across 3 availability zones.
- Routers start at $6 (NKR-0). Production router compute = rate × observed routers ÷ 3, one router per AZ.
- Four PS-20 shards plus NKR-20 routers: 4 × $50 + $170 × 3 ÷ 3 = $370/month, before storage and backups.

PlanetScale says preview is not for production, and that "some of those changes will be breaking".

The second bet is quieter. In March 2026 PlanetScale hired Drizzle's entire core team; Drizzle's own page calls PlanetScale its "biggest sponsor". If you write Drizzle, your ORM's maintainers work for one of these two vendors.

sections.title: Pick Neon if your databases sleep at night; pick PlanetScale if they never do
sections.content:
If your dev and test databases sit idle overnight and every pull request gets a branch, pick Neon: suspended hours bill $0 and 20 branches cost $15 in fees, not $300 in clusters. If production must stay awake on a bill that does not move with the clock, or you run a Vitess-shaped MySQL estate, pick PlanetScale. Neki is not a decision yet, because it is a preview.

Check this today:

1. Pull last month's awake hours per Neon compute. A 0.25 CU compute above 566 hours already costs more than PS-5 HA.
2. Count branches alive at once and how long each lives, and price them as PlanetScale clusters before copying the habit.
3. Find whatever pings your database more often than every five minutes. That probe, not your traffic, decides which vendor is cheaper.

decision_matrix.situation: Dev and test databases idle overnight, one branch per pull request
decision_matrix.why: Suspended compute bills $0 and branches past the included 10 cost $1.50 per branch-month instead of a cluster each.

decision_matrix.situation: Steady production awake 24/7 with a budget that must not move
decision_matrix.why: A flat SKU such as PS-5 HA at $15 undercuts 0.25 CU awake all month on Neon Launch at $19.35.
Neon's pricing lists only Lakebase Postgres, so leaving Vitess would be an engine migration, not a vendor switch.

decision_matrix.situation: Side project or prototype with a $0 budget
decision_matrix.why: PlanetScale has no free plan, while Neon Free is permanent, needs no card and includes 100 CU-hours per project.

decision_matrix.situation: Postgres that needs horizontal sharding in production this quarter
decision_matrix.why: Neki is a platform preview and PlanetScale says not to run production on it.

decision_matrix.situation: Compliance-bound production (HIPAA BAA, uptime SLA) with traffic that idles for hours
decision_matrix.why: Scale includes self-serve HIPAA with a BAA and an SLA while still suspending idle compute, so quiet hours bill $0 at the $0.222 rate.

decision_matrix.situation: One CU of production awake more than 667 hours a month on Neon Scale
decision_matrix.why: Past $148 ÷ $0.222 = 667 hours, the flat $148 cluster is the cheaper meter.

decision_matrix.situation: Production already on Neon that suspends every night
decision_matrix.why: Every suspended hour is $0 on Neon that a PlanetScale cluster would bill at its flat rate.

cost_math.label: Always-on small database, Neon Launch vs PlanetScale PS-5 HA
One CU all month, Neon Launch / Neon Scale vs PlanetScale PS-80 HA (arm64)
Neki: four PS-20 shards plus production routers

verdict_summary: Neon wins if your dev and test databases sleep at night and every pull request gets a branch, because suspended compute bills $0 and branch fees replace whole clusters. PlanetScale wins if production must stay awake on a bill that does not move with the clock, or if you already run Vitess-shaped MySQL. Neki is a platform preview, so sharded Postgres on PlanetScale is not a production decision yet.

faqs.q: Does Neon Launch come with an uptime SLA?
faqs.a: No; Launch has no SLA. The uptime SLA, HIPAA with a BAA, SOC 2 and ISO 27001/27701 arrive with Scale, along with private networking at $0.01/GB.

faqs.q: What does 100 GB of storage cost?
faqs.a: On Neon Launch it is 100 × $0.35 = $35/month. PlanetScale includes 10 GB per instance and bills the rest at a region volume rate it publishes only through an endpoint, on the primary and both replicas of an HA cluster.

Neon Launch includes 500 GB per project, then $0.10/GB. PlanetScale includes 100 GB/month on a production branch and 10 GB on development branches and PS-5 non-HA, then a region rate it does not print; ingress is free.

faqs.q: Can I start on Neki unsharded and shard later?
faqs.a: Yes: PlanetScale lists resharding, schema changes, version upgrades and failovers as online workflows, so you can start unsharded and reshard later. Existing drivers, ORMs and connection strings keep working because the router speaks the standard Postgres wire protocol.
